rationale: PINS the tenth relationship type, `references`, and the resolution gate that decides what it publishes. Dart is statically typed: a type POSITION is grammatical (`type_identifier` never appears where a value identifier appears), so 'this declaration mentions that type' is a parse fact rather than a capitalization convention. Before this the analyzer read type positions only into the symbol payload (returnType, parameters[].type, dataType) and published NO edge for any of them, so the type graph of a Dart codebase was unread. The gate is resolution, and it is the design rather than an apology: over 1,000 corpus files in 5 repositories there are 75,769 type mentions outside heritage clauses and only 3,460 (4.57%) name a type the same file declares. The other 95.43% name `String`, `Widget`, `Future` — real types in dart:core and the Flutter SDK, declared in files a per-file run has not read. Publishing them would make the label mostly a list of SDK type names at roughly 22x the edge count, every one an endpoint no symbol in the index can bind. Each forbid below names a shape where a plausible widening either double-counts a fact another label already carries or claims a mention the source does not make.

expectRelationships.note: THE CONFIDENCE PIN, and the reason it is an exact equality rather than a floor. The MENTION is a parse fact — `type_identifier` is a grammatical position — but the BINDING of that name to a declaration is not, so 0.95 and not 1.0. Publishing it at 1.0 would claim the analyzer can see every declaration a Dart program names, which is exactly what the resolution gate below says it cannot. A `confidenceMin` row is satisfied by 1.0 and therefore proves nothing here; this one is not.
POSITIVE 1: a RETURN type, the simplest shape there is and the one a pass reading only parameter lists would miss.

POSITIVE 4: a type in a CONSTRUCTOR's parameter list. The source is the family name `constructor`, so a change that started naming the segment (`Wallet.adopted`) would break this pin while `contains` kept saying `constructor` — the two labels have to agree on the identity of a constructor or a graph cannot join them.

POSITIVE 2: a PARAMETER type, and the row that makes the resolution gate visible — this method's parameters also mention `String`, which no file here declares, and that mention publishes nothing. Without the gate this row and the `String` forbid below would be indistinguishable.
POSITIVE 3: a TYPE ARGUMENT (`List<Wallet>`) — a mention in the written type and in the literal `<Wallet>[]`, deduped to one row.
POSITIVE 5: a TYPE TEST and a TYPE CAST (`other is Wallet`, `other as Wallet`) — two node types, one row after dedup.
POSITIVE 6: an `on T` CATCH clause plus a cast in the same method.

POSITIVE 7: a RECORD FIELD TYPE. Dart 3 record types already had to be added to three type extractors in this lane, so the type MENTION position is pinned too: a record type whose fields were dropped would leave this row missing.

POSITIVE 13, and the row that draws the boundary between two labels over ONE expression. `Derived make() => Derived(...)` MENTIONS the type (its return type) and CONSTRUCTS it, so this method publishes a `references` row AND an `instantiates` row to the same target. They are different facts and both are true; collapsing them would lose either the dependency or the construction.
POSITIVE 8: a TYPE BOUND (`class Box<T extends Wallet>`). The bound names a real type and publishes — the positive half of the pair that makes the type-variable forbids mean something.

POSITIVE 9: a TYPEDEF's aliased type. The SOURCE is the alias symbol, not the file: attributing it to the file basename would be a claim about a module that declares nothing, and no symbol in the index is named after the file.
POSITIVE 10: a NAMED extension's `on` clause. No other label carries an extension's target type.
POSITIVE 11: a parameter type naming a declared ENUM. An enum is a type in Dart; it is the enum's MEMBERS that `uses` reads, not the enum.

POSITIVE 12: a LOCAL declaration's type, a closure parameter's type and a for-in element type, all folded into the enclosing function because a local is not a published symbol (DARTD8 parity). The dedup key collapses them into one row, so this pin also asserts that exactly one survived.

forbidRelationships.note: THE DOUBLE-COUNT PIN. `class Derived extends Wallet` already publishes `Derived extends Wallet` at confidence 1.0. A `references` edge for the same base counts one inheritance fact twice under two labels — the same defect class as a mislabel, in the other direction.
`implements Wallet` is already `implements`, and this class also `extends Wallet`, so the pin cannot be satisfied by suppressing only the `extends` spelling.
A `with` clause is already its own relationship (`mixes_in` since 2026-10-18; `uses{isMixin}` before). Publishing it as a type reference would duplicate the mixin dependency.

THE CONSTRUCTION PIN. `buildOnly` CONSTRUCTS a Wallet and names no type at all, so the construction is `instantiates` and `references` has nothing to say. A pass that read call sites as type mentions would add this row — and `Wallet` IS declared in this file, which is exactly what makes that mistake easy.

THE TYPE-VARIABLE PIN. `class Box<T extends Wallet>` DECLARES a type variable; `T get()` MENTIONS the variable, which is not a declared type. Publishing it would make every generic class appear to depend on a type it introduced itself.
The same variable in a PARAMETER position and inside a method BODY rather than a signature, so a shadow check that only looked at signatures would pass the `get` pin and fail here.
The variable mentioned at the TYPE-PARAMETER DECLARATION itself: `type_parameter` is the one position where a `type_identifier` names nothing that exists outside the declaration introducing it.

THE LOOSE-BOUNDED TYPE-VARIABLE PIN, and the one that makes the three above load-bearing rather than incidental. `class T` is a REAL type declared in this file, so `T? cached` inside `class Shadowed<T extends Shadowed>` RESOLVES — to the wrong declaration. Only refusing a name an ancestor introduced as a type parameter stops `Shadowed` from depending on a type it shadows. Removing that check leaves every other pin in this file green, which is what makes this row the one that holds it.

THE SELF-REFERENCE PIN, and it is about a real Dart feature rather than a hypothetical: the UNNAMED extension below is published under its target type's name, so `extension on Wallet {}` has source Wallet and mentions Wallet. A self-dependency is not a dependency.

THE RESOLUTION GATE. `String` is written in this file (a parameter type, a field type), is a real class in dart:core, and is declared in no file here — so there is nothing for the edge to bind to. This is 95.43% of the corpus's type mentions.
And on the BASE of a type argument. `List<Wallet>` mentions two types; this row proves the gate applies to each independently — `Wallet` publishes (POSITIVE 3) while `List` does not.

The same gate on a RETURN type: `Widget` is written here, is a real Flutter class, and is declared in no file in this fixture. A pass that resolved mentions against the whole word list instead of the declared-TYPE set would publish it.

`dynamic` is Dart's IMPLICIT type — the absence of a declared type, not a dependency on one. It is spelled as a type name in the grammar, so a pass with no explicit exclusion reads it as a mention, and the `dynamic raw` parameter above is what makes this row load-bearing rather than inert.

R7 CROSS-PIN: no relationship of ANY label may carry the placeholder literal `unknown` as an endpoint. The corpus shape that produced 106 such rows on this lane's 2,735-file sample (239 on proxicall's full tracked set) is in the `unknown-endpoint-r7` fixture.

_pin_key_note: Keys are the ones script/m14/run-fixtures.ts reads — expectSymbols, expectRelationships, forbidRelationships — with `note` as documentation (CONSTRAINT_DOC_KEYS) and `confidenceMin` on the allowlist. An unknown top-level key is not a failing pin, it is an INERT one: it asserts nothing and reads as coverage. The last forbid omits `type` deliberately, so it matches an endpoint pair under any label.
